one_line: Market volatility, political pushback over infrastructure, and new theoretical research dominate industry developments.

themes.title: Financial and political headwinds hit AI
themes.text: Wall Street experienced a $5.7 trillion market rout as doubts grew over AI spending payoffs, while Jefferies warned that the global investment cycle may have peaked. Meanwhile, midterm election results led to voter rejections of data centers and policy shifts from OpenAI regarding local infrastructure expansion.

stories.headline: Wall Street grapples with $5.7 trillion rout as AI bets unwind
AI investment cycle may have peaked, Jefferies warns
After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
OpenAI changes data center policies after midterm voter pushback
Anthropic-backed PAC Public First spent $63M+ in 2026 midterms

themes.title: New research and memory architectures
themes.text: OpenAI and Anthropic models disproved the 27-year-old Exponential Time Hypothesis, and Anthropic detailed a new agent memory architecture with a 'dreaming' process. Meta also introduced Active Memory and Active Focus updates for its Muse and Meta AI users.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic AI models disprove Exponential Time Hypothesis
Anthropic details agent memory architecture and dreaming capability
Meta brings Active Memory and Active Focus to Muse and Meta AI

themes.title: Security vulnerabilities and exposed tools
themes.text: Censys discovered over 800 publicly exposed copies of the Chinese-made ARTEX penetration testing tool. Separately, security researchers found that Claude Code approval files inadvertently stored database passwords and credentials in public GitHub repositories.

stories.headline: Censys discovers 800+ publicly exposed copies of ARTEX AI hacking tool
Claude Code approval files expose company secrets on GitHub
